chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I would prefer to bequeath one-fifth of my wealth than to bequeath one-quarter, and I would prefer to bequeath one-quarter than to bequeath one-third. And whoever bequeaths one-third has not left anything [for heirs] and has reached the limit [of excess].'
He said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man who died and bequeathed all or most of his wealth, saying to him:

The bequest is returned to the reasonable [limit], excluding the excessive. Whoever wrongs himself and includes the excessive and the deviation in his bequest, then it is returned to the reasonable limit, and the heirs are left with their inheritance.
ai.seo_question: What is the preferred and maximum limit for bequest (wasiyyah) in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that Imam Ali (peace be upon him) preferred bequeathing one-fifth over one-quarter, and one-quarter over one-third, noting that bequeathing the full one-third leaves little for heirs. The text establishes the legal ruling that a bequest exceeding the reasonable limit (typically one-third) is reduced to that limit, preserving the heirs' rights, unless the bequeather intended to give more but was not excessive in a way that wronged them. This narration highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on balancing the testator's autonomy with the mandatory rights of heirs, reflecting the principle of 'al-ma'ruf' (the reasonable/known standard) in inheritance law.
